title: Swe senior systemdesign observability
question: You're introducing observability standards for a growing set of microservices where right now every team logs however they want and there's no way to trace a request across services. How do you design this?
idealAnswer:
Distinguishes the three pillars and what each is actually for: structured logs for detailed event context, metrics for aggregate trends and alerting, distributed traces for following one request's path and timing across services

Centers distributed tracing as the key piece for this specific problem, propagating a trace/correlation id through every hop (including async work like queue messages) so a single user action can be reconstructed across all five or six services it touches

Proposes structured logging with a consistent schema (e.g. shared fields like request id, service name, severity) enforced across teams, rather than each team's free-form log format, so logs are actually queryable together

Addresses the org/adoption problem, not just the technical one, e.g. a shared library or sidecar that makes correlation ids and standard fields the path of least resistance, since fifteen independently-owned services won't adopt a standard just because it's documented somewhere

Mentions defining what to alert on, e.g. SLO-based alerting on user-facing symptoms (latency, error rate) rather than every team inventing its own alert thresholds, and connects metrics/traces together so an alert can lead directly to the relevant traces
